items.prose: A pot of £1.00 doubles every day.
items.question: How much does it hold after 8 days?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply by 2 once for each of the 8 days.

byKey.times: You multiplied 2 by 8. Eight doublings multiply by 2 eight times over.
byKey.swap: You worked out $8^2$. The base is 2 and the power is 8.
byKey.seven: You stopped one doubling short. Day 0 holds £1.00, so day 8 is eight doublings.

explain.text: Eight doublings multiply by $2^8 = 256$, so the pot holds £256.00.

items.prose: A share falls 7% in a day.
items.question: What factor multiplies its price?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtract the fall, as a decimal, from 1.

byKey.rate: You wrote the part lost. The factor is the part kept: $1 - 0.07$.
byKey.plus: You added the 7%. A fall subtracts.

explain.text: A 7% fall keeps 93% of the price, so the factor is 0.93.

widget.label: Value of 4 to the power minus 1

feedback.generic: Not quite right. A power of −1 means one over the number.

byKey.neg: You made the 4 negative. The minus in the power means one over: $\tfrac{1}{4}$.
byKey.tenth: You turned 4 into 0.4. One over 4 is 0.25.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. A step left undoes one step of decay.

byKey.same: You used $x = 1$. At $x = -1$ the power is negative, so the height is one over 0.25.
byKey.neg: You made the height negative. Exponential curves stay above the x-axis.

explain.text: $0.25^{-1} = \tfrac{1}{0.25} = 4$. Decay to the right is growth to the left.

items.prose: £5,000.00 earns 4% a year, compounded, for 3 years.
items.question: What is the balance after 3 years?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply by 1.04 once for each year.

byKey.simple: You added £200.00 a year. Each year's 4% is of a bigger balance, so you lost the interest on interest.
byKey.one: That is after one year. Apply 1.04 three times.
byKey.two: That is after two years. Apply 1.04 once more.

explain.text: $1.04^3 = 1.124864$, so the balance is £5,624.32. Simple interest would give £5,600.00; the extra £24.32 is interest on interest.

widget.label: Value of 32 to the power three fifths

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the fifth root, then cube it.

byKey.times: You multiplied 32 by $\tfrac{3}{5}$. The 5 picks a fifth root and the 3 cubes it.
byKey.root: You took the fifth root and stopped. Cube it too.

items.prose: A share rose steadily from £10.00 to £30.00 in 6 years, at a constant yearly rate.
items.question: At the same rate, how many more years does it take to reach £90.00?

feedback.correct: 6 years: every tripling takes the same time.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the factor from £30.00 to £90.00 with the first one.

byKey.linear: You gave each pound the same time: £20.00 per 6 years. Growth here is by a factor, and £30.00 triples as fast as £10.00.
byKey.total: That counts from the start. The question asks for more years after £30.00.

explain.text: £10.00 to £30.00 is a factor of 3 in 6 years. £30.00 to £90.00 is the same factor, so it takes the same 6 years.

items.prose: Ten doublings multiply by $2^{10} = 1024$, about a thousand.
items.question: About how many times bigger is something after 20 doublings?

options.why: You doubled the thousand because the doublings doubled. The second ten multiply by about a thousand again.
You multiplied the thousand by 10. Twenty doublings are two blocks of ten: a thousand times a thousand.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Split twenty doublings into two blocks of ten.

explain.text: $2^{20} = 1048576$, about a million. Each block of ten doublings multiplies by about a thousand.

items.prose: A strategy loses 2% of its capital every trading day.
items.question: After how many whole days is less than half the capital left?

widget.label: Days until under half
widget.accept: 35. After 34 days 50.3% is left; after 35 days, 49.3%.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the first $n$ with $0.98^n < 0.5$.

byKey.linear: You lost 2% of the start each day: 25 days to lose half. Each loss is 2% of what is left, so it takes longer.
byKey.close: After 34 days $0.98^{34} \approx 0.503$ is left, still just over half.

explain.text: Each day multiplies by 0.98. $0.98^{34} \approx 0.503$ and $0.98^{35} \approx 0.493$, so day 35 is the first under half. Decay is slower than steady loss.

items.prose: A price grows by a factor of 1.5 each year. It is £27.00 now.
items.question: What was it 3 years ago?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Going back 3 years divides by 1.5 three times.

byKey.divlin: You divided by $1.5 \times 3$. Three years back divide by 1.5 three times: by $1.5^3 = 3.375$.
byKey.forward: You went forward 3 years. Back in time uses the power −3.
byKey.subtract: You took off half of £27.00 each year in a line. Each year back divides by 1.5.

explain.text: Three years back is the power −3: $27 \times 1.5^{-3} = 27 \div 3.375 = 8$. Check forward: $8 \times 1.5^3 = 27$.
